A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
entrainment mapping is a powerful tool in the identification of reentrant circuits.

during entrainment, the return cycle length is the best indicator of whether the recording site is within a reentry circuit, but the return cycle length may be misleading when the recording and paced sites are not the same.

during entrainment of ventricular tachyarrhythmias with analysis of electrogram timing at the pacing site, the relation of the electrogram to the QRS complexes and the return cycle are not useful in identifying reentry circuit sites when the recording and the pacing sites are separate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relation between an electrogram recorded during entrainment and the QRS complex is not always indicative of its position relative to the reentry site.
entrainment analysis should be performed from the same site as the pacing site to accurately identify reentry circuit locations.

during entrainment of ventricular tachyarrhythmias, it is not possible to determine with certainty whether an electrogram recorded from an area of abnormal electrical activity reflects activation times in the reentry circuit, or in bystander areas of abnormal electrical conduction.
